la:verb:pernosco.html:
per-nosco, ōvi, ōtum, 3, v. a.
To examine thoroughly: pernoscite, Furtumne factum existimetis, an, etc.,.—Hence, in perf., to have examined or discerned, to know thoroughly, to become thoroughly acquainted with, to get a correct knowledge of: ingenium avidi haud pernoram hospitis,: facta pernovit probe,: pernovi equidem ingenium tuum ingenuom admodum,.—
To learn thor

oughly, become fully acquainted with: hominum mores ex corpore, oculis, vultu, etc., pernoscere,: motus animorum sunt penitus oratori pernoscendi,.—Hence, pernōtus, a, um, P. a., thoroughly known, well known: pugil ob eximiam virtutem virium regi pernotus et gratus,; ; .

la:verb:pernego.html:
per-nĕgo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
To deny altogether; to deny steadily, stoutly, or flatly: Negas? Ly. Pernego immo, : pernegabo atque obdurabo,: saepe appellati, pernegaverunt,: pyxidem traditam pernegaret,; .—
To refuse or decline altogether (postAug.): Catoni populus Romanus praeturam negavit, consulatum pernegavit,; .
